text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly selling Stock D and Stock E after gains felt rewarding, but I should trim only when it fits my target allocation or risk plan—not simply to lock in a profit.","Selling Stock B at a loss was painful, yet holding or selling should depend on its prospects and portfolio role, not on avoiding a realized loss or returning to my average cost.","Buying Stock C and later seeing the account dip reminded me that a single trade need not pay off immediately; I should size purchases prudently, preserve diversification, and avoid reacting to short-term moves."]}
